Hi Kenji / Aya,

Thanks again for the interest in Redwood — really excited to show how we can tighten inference latency for your batch processing pipelines. I pulled a few 30-min windows that work for our APAC engineering pair (Marissa + myself):

- Mon Jan 10, 10:00–10:30 JST (09:00 SGT / 11:00 AEST)
- Mon Jan 10, 15:00–15:30 JST (14:00 SGT / 16:00 AEST)
- Tue Jan 11, 09:00–09:30 JST (08:00 SGT / 10:00 AEST)

If any of those look good, I’ll send a calendar invite. Note: our Calendly sometimes surfaces times in recipients’ calendar apps as the previous day when the viewer is in the US — we’ll pin the timezone explicitly to avoid confusion. I’ve attached a one-pager for quick context.

Also copying Marissa (customer success) who’ll be on the call.

Best,

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the options. 10:00 JST on Jan 10 looks best for us. Quick thing — when I clicked the Calendly link it showed the invite as ‘Sun, Jan 9, 10:00 PM’ in my Google Calendar (screenshot attached). That made me pause because that’s the previous day in the US time zone. Can you confirm the event will be Jan 10 at 10:00 AM JST?

Aya and I are both in Tokyo and want to be sure we don’t accidentally accept the wrong date.

—Kenji

Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2027 01:05:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Scheduling: Quick demo for Redwood Inference — Tokyo/Singapore window

Hi Kenji — good catch and sorry for the confusion.

What happened: our Calendly was set to display invite times in the visitor’s detected timezone, but we also had a legacy setting that showed the organizer’s (US/PST) day in some previews — that’s why you saw Jan 9 in the preview pane. The actual meeting time is Jan 10 at 10:00 JST (2027-01-10T10:00:00+09:00). I’ll send an explicit ICS invite with the timezone pinned to Asia/Tokyo so Google/Outlook shows the correct local date.

If it helps, here’s the explicit mapping:
- 10:00 JST (Tokyo) = 09:00 SGT (Singapore) = 11:00 AEDT (Sydney) = 18:00 PST (previous day)

I’m attaching the one-pager again and will follow up with the ICS + calendar invite. Does Jan 10 10:00 JST work for your team?

Thanks,
Ben
On behalf of the Redwood APAC team.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kenji Saito <k.saito@aquavista.co.jp>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2027 12:10:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Scheduling: Quick demo for Redwood Inference — Tokyo/Singapore window

Hi Kenji — happy to jump on this call. If you prefer an earlier slot the same day we also have 08:30 JST available (07:30 SGT / 09:30 AEST). No worries either way — we’ll make sure the invite shows the local date/time clearly.

Ben — when you send the ICS can you explicitly set the timezone to Asia/Tokyo and include the meeting text: “Redwood — Demo (APAC) — Jan 10, 10:00–10:30 JST”. That prevents calendar clients from rendering the US previous-day label.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
